instrument snapshot (`OKTContractInstrumentSnapshot.is_xperps`, itself
sourced from the Rust `is_x_perps_pair()` classification). The red dot and
USD settlement ccy are self-sourced from Rust (red-dot use case +
`trade_setting`). Non-X-Perp pairs return the inert default (plain "+", no
dot, no settlement row), so the caller can apply this unconditionally on
every instrument change without branching.

`key_feature_available_icon` on Kotlin's `TradeAbTestManager`). When true,

renders the default plus icon — but `show_settle_gear` stays true for

Gray SDK is a native input (no Rust producer for AB values), so the flag
is passed in rather than read here — mirrors the `is_lite` / `is_cr_market`
native-input convention elsewhere in this crate.
`is_xperps` / `is_usd_um` come from the caller's instrument snapshot
(`OKTContractInstrumentSnapshot`). Both branches share the gear icon + red
dot + settlement-ccy row because they consume the same USDⓈ-M settle ccy
source (`get_usd_settle_ccy`); the red-dot use case (SP key) is shared, so
a user who dismisses the dot on one branch will not see it re-appear on the
other. Pairs outside the class return the inert default (plain "+", no dot,
no settlement row), so the caller can invoke this unconditionally on every
instrument change without branching.

doc:
View object for the reverse position confirmation page

Contains all formatted data ready for UI display.
Maps 1:1 to the page UI sections.

# Page Layout

```text
+-----------------------------------------------------------+
| [TopBar] Reverse Position                     [X]         |
+-----------------------------------------------------------+
| [TopInfo]                                                 |
|   "BTC-USDT Perp"  [Isolated]  [Short to Long]           |  <- inst_name, margin_mode, reverse_direction
|   Latest Price: 65,230.5                                  |  <- (native ticker, NOT in VO)
+-----------------------------------------------------------+
| [Origin Position]                                         |
|   | Market Buy                                            |  <- origin_entrust_state
|   | [Buy 20x]                                             |  <- origin_side, origin_lever
|   | Close amount        100 Cont                          |  <- origin_close_size (from API)
|   | Order price         Market                            |  <- (static)
+-------------- [Short to Long] ----------------------------+  <- middle_direction_text
| [After Reverse]                                           |
|   | Market Sell                                           |  <- reverse_entrust_state
|   | [Sell]                                                |  <- reverse_side
|   | Est. open amount    100 Cont                          |  <- reverse_open_size (from API)
|   | Order price         Market                            |  <- (static)
|   | Est. liq price      45,000 USDT (2.00%)              |  <- reverse_liq_price + reverse_price_gap
|   | Leverage            10x                               |  <- reverse_leverage (from API)
+-----------------------------------------------------------+
| [Tip Note]                                                |
+-----------------------------------------------------------+
| [ ] Do not show again                                     |
| [Confirm Reverse]                                         |
+-----------------------------------------------------------+
```

# iOS Reference

- `OKTPReverseCheckTopInfoVC` -> top info section
- `OKTPReverseOriginPositionInfoVC` -> origin position section
- `OKTPRPartingLineShowView` -> middle direction arrow
- `OKTPRAfterReverseInfoVC` -> after reverse section

# Usage

```ignore
let vo = manager.pre_check(&position).await?;

// Top info
instNameLabel.text = vo.inst_name
marginModeTag.text = native_localize(vo.margin_mode)  // "isolated" -> "Isolated"
reverseDirectionTag.text = native_direction_label(vo)  // uses pos_side + inst_type

// Origin position (formatted values)
closeSizeLabel.text = vo.origin_close_size.toString()

// After reverse (formatted values from API)
openSizeLabel.text = vo.reverse_open_size.toString()
liqPriceLabel.text = vo.reverse_liq_price.toString()

// Dialog decisions
if vo.is_leverage_changed { showLeverageMismatchDialog(...) }
if !vo.is_full_reverse { showPartialReverseDialog(...) }
```

name: set_attach_inst_id
doc:
GAP A root fix (2026-07-31): re-feed the LIVE `inst_id` into `ctx` after the
instrument settles. The attach binder is created early (fragment
onViewCreated) when the snapshot instId is not yet ready, so `init.inst_id`
(and thus `ctx.inst_id`) is empty; `set_contract_facevalue` re-feeds
ctVal/isInverse but NOT inst_id. With `ctx.inst_id` empty, `resolve_inst_family`
fails and profit_dig / price_digit / `to_base_for_order` all fall back
(inverse dual-pnl "--" + wrong precision). Kotlin calls this from
`PureTPSLViewBinder` alongside `set_contract_facevalue` with the live
`cachedInstId`, so once the instrument settles the dual-pnl compute resolves
the real per-family profit precision, tick precision, and inverse convertor.
Empty input is ignored (never clobber a good id with a bootstrap-race empty).
Additive FFI — iOS need not call it (no signature change).

name: query_settle_collateral_relation
doc:
Query the enable-relation state for `ccy` before silently enabling it as
collateral (settle-ccy auto-enable, Rust cohort). Fetches the current
collateral assets and reports whether the caller must prompt the user to
also enable relation partners.

The `needs_prompt` rule mirrors the open-collateral interactor's
`enable_relation_prompt` (V1 `handleRelatedCoin(ccy, isOpened = true)`)
exactly: the base coin must have enable-relation partners AND at least one
of them must currently NOT be collateral-enabled. A partner that is missing
from the fetched assets list does NOT count toward the prompt
(`unwrap_or(false)`), matching the interactor's rule.

No submit / no state mutation — pure query. On success returns
`SettleCollateralRelationVo { needs_prompt, relation_ccys }`; the caller
decides which coins to pass to `enable_collateral_coins`.

name: sl_liq_warning_key_at_confirm
doc:
Stage-2 of the SL-vs-liquidation warning: the ORDER-CONFIRM sheet's place-order
button. Empty string = no warning.

Native `OkTradePresenter.tradeOrderConfirm`:883-893 runs a SECOND check when the
confirm sheet's button is tapped, and deliberately uses a DIFFERENT, fresher
liquidation source than the panel stage: `checkData.liqPx`, i.e. the pre-check
response's estimate rather than the panel's max-available pair. That is why the panel
stage alone is not equivalent -- when the max-available snapshot carries no liq price
(native explicitly passes "" while the balance request is in flight,
`AbsFutureTradePanelPresenter`:2691-2696), native still catches the crossing here.

Suppression mirrors native's `group.optional.disableSlLiqTip`: that flag is set
exactly when the panel stage SHOWED its dialog and the user confirmed, and it makes
stage 2 skip so the user never sees two dialogs for one order. The frozen
`attached_tpsl_sl_liq_warning_key` on this attempt is the equivalent signal -- it is
non-empty if and only if the panel stage warned (and had the user chosen the
change-price button instead of place-order, no confirm sheet would exist to reach
this method).

Gated on the bare `get_liq_px_confirm()` like native, NOT on the confirm sheet's
`liq_shown` row-visibility flag -- that one additionally requires single/cross and
non-close, an intentional V2-only narrowing of the row projection which must not leak
into this gate. No dynamic-ratio fallback: native's stage 2 reads only the static
`attachSp.firstOrNull { it.slTriggerPx.gt(0) }`.

name: pure_fetch_deposit_prefill
doc:
Kernel deposit-prefill (PREFER path): self-source the decision flags from
Rust producers, fetch the asset valuation via Rust, and produce a complete
[`PureDepositPrefill`].

**Rust-self-source contract (no Kotlin round-trip)**: 5 of the 6 V1 decision
flags + `currency_id` are derived inside [`resolve_deposit_decision_flags`]
straight from OKCore producers (feature-restriction / account-manager /
settings currency-list / coin-wrapper). Native does NOT precompute any of
those with a legacy API and hand it back (that is the fake round-trip the
phase-4 audit gate bans).

The exported "+" launcher keeps `is_cr_market` as an input for wire
compatibility with its existing caller. Normal-order error recovery does
not use that input: [`build_order_error_deposit_prefill`] reads the Rust
app-mode provider directly before projecting the navigation payload.

The valuation fetch mirrors V1 `FundTransferBtnDelegate.requestAPI()` →
`FundTransInTradingPageUseCase(currencyId)` (POST
`/v2/asset/accounts/user-currency-list-balance`), already ported as
`QueryUserBalanceUseCase`. On API error / empty / `currency_id == 0` the
valuation is `None`, matching V1's error path (which routes through
`goToDepositPageDefault` — equivalent to the priority-5 fallback arm of the
option tree, where `asset_amount = None`).

`cancel_token` follows the standard async-export convention (see
`ct_fetch_entity_upgrade_state`).

#2a (device recvqck62xDPO0) contract attached-TPSL direction-validity gate,
invoked by the 6 contract make-order fragments BEFORE the confirm sheet.
V1 mirror `OkTradeFuturePresent.checkSimpleTpSl` + `AbsFutureTradePanelPresenter

limit-flag param is needed.

R-MIG-370 DEEP #1: also projects the resolved-token string into the
typed `state.td_mode` (`OKTSpotTdMode`) consumed by `derive_can_borrow`
Path-1 (`td_mode == Cross`), then re-runs the native can_borrow derive.

Copy-trade fix (device 2026-07-15): the Kotlin host resolves the non-multi
-attr value via `OrderLeadUtils.getSpotMgn` → `getOrderLeaderSwitchStatusList()`,
but that Kotlin `TradeConfig` switch-status list is NOT populated in Pure V2
— the close-switch SSOT moved to the Rust `inst_config_info` cache (written
by `ct_container_manager::set_lead_switch` / `trade_facade`). With an empty
Kotlin list `!contains(instId)` is always true, so `getSpotMgn` returned
`spot_isolated` for EVERY spot-lead stop order regardless of the close-follow
switch (single + double, buy + sell). Re-derive `getSpotMgn` here from the
populated Rust SSOT — native contract `OrderLeadUtils.kt:60-62`:
`isOrderLeaderSpotPosition(instId) && orderLeaderSwitchOpen(instId)` where
`orderLeaderSwitchOpen = isOrderLeaderSpotPosition && !close_switch_list
.contains(instId)` (R7: `close_switch_list` holds lead-CLOSED instIds, so
lead-on = NOT in the list). The multi-attr (MCC/PM) branch keeps the
Kotlin-pushed margin mode (cross/isolated), which this bug does not affect.
CTRSTrade globals are read OUTSIDE `modify_state` (ct_container_manager §A).

the header at `on_visible` and live-updated by the ticker subscription so
the row is never a raw-USD number on a coin-margined instrument (B6).
The RAW base last-price used for order/percent math lives on the session
shadow (`session.last_price()`), not here.

fields.name: session_id
fields.doc:
Monotonic session epoch — bumped on every `on_visible`. Every async
task captures the value at spawn-time and skips the State write when
it no longer matches (mirror of close-position §J.1 / §J.4 guard).

fields.name: input_price
fields.doc:
Current price-input value. §D: this is business runtime input state, so
it flows through State (mirror of close-position `state.input_price`)
rather than a `RwLock<String>` struct field that observers can't see.
Native echoes the same value back via the controlled input.

fields.name: input_amount
fields.doc:
Current amount-input value. §D: business runtime input state through
State (same rationale as `input_price`).

fields.name: amount_unit_label
fields.doc:
Current trade-unit chip label (contract / coin / U) for the amount input,
resolved from the bound context's `trade_unit` via the shared contract
unit-option builder. Native renders it as the amount-input unit suffix.
mirror Native ContractAmountInputComponent unit chip.

fields.name: amount_unit_options
fields.doc:
Selectable trade-unit rows (contract / coin / U) for the unit-switch bottom
sheet, built by the canonical
`render::derive_amount_unit_options` (same shape the order-entry panels
feed to `ContractAmountUnitSwitchSheet`). Empty until the session is
bound / the instrument snapshot resolves.

fields.name: amount_box_display
fields.doc:
BUG1: amount-box display literal in slider (percent) mode, e.g. "25%".
Empty in typed mode (native then echoes `input_amount` into the box).
Native parity: the seekbar shows the "N%" literal on the box and carries
the resolved size on `input_amount` (submit reads `input_amount`, never
this literal). Additive field appended for forward-compat.

fields.name: order_amount_hint
fields.doc:
BUG2: place-button "approx" hint line, e.g. "~=0.0837 BTC". Placeholder
when there is no active percent / size selection. Mirror native
TradeSeekBarViewBinder.generateText approximation line. Additive field.

fields.name: bbo_warning_accepted_for_submit
fields.doc:
One-shot acknowledgement for the local contract BBO warning. It is
consumed by the next submit attempt and never survives panel teardown.

name: margin_mode_set_multi_inst
doc:
Mirrors Kotlin `setMultiInstMarginModes(marginMode, instFamilyList, instTypeList, listener, accountMode)`.

Fan-outs into one `sync_margin_mode` call per inst_type entry. If
`inst_family_list` is non-empty for that inst_type, it is passed through.
